answer.text: Sell an OTM call and an OTM put, while buying a further OTM call and a further OTM put — it creates a range-bound income strategy with all four positions limiting risk. Max profit = net premium received. Max loss = width of either spread minus net premium
Buy four options at four different strikes for maximum flexibility

explanation.text: The Logic: An iron condor is a four-leg, range-bound, defined-risk strategy: short one OTM call, long a further OTM call, short one OTM put, and long a further OTM put — all on the same underlying and expiry. It is structurally a short OTM call spread combined with a short OTM put spread, entered for a net credit. Maximum profit equals the net premium received (if the underlying stays between the two short strikes), and maximum loss on either wing equals the wing width minus the net premium received. The Trap: An iron condor has exactly four specifically chosen legs (two credit vertical spreads), not "four random strikes," not two bull spreads, and not a short straddle hedged with the underlying. The defining features are the two short OTM options that create the income and the two further-OTM long options that cap the loss on each side.
